extracted.intended_audience: SFWA members; authors, creators, editors, publishers, and agents of science fiction & fantasy works considering Nebula Awards submission or participation
extracted.subtask_description: Complete official rules governing eligibility, category definitions, nominations, voting, withdrawals, recusal and appeals, and award administration for the SFWA Nebula Awards (effective for award year beginning Jan 1, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories and length definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nebula Awards® will be made in the following categories: Short Story: fewer than 7,500 words; Novelette: at least 7,500 words but fewer than 17,500 words; Novella: at least 17,500 words but fewer than 40,000 words; Novel: 40,000 words or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit word-count thresholds define which category a prose work belongs to for eligibility and nomination purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Andre Norton Award definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Andre Norton Award for Middle Grade and Young Adult Fiction: Middle grade or young adult science fiction or fantasy (or related genre) books of any length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible works include middle grade or young adult SF/F books regardless of length; graphic novels may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game Writing definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Game Writing: An interactive or playable story-driven work of any length which conveys narrative, character, or story background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Game Writing category is for interactive/playable works that convey story; later guidance clarifies wordless games can be eligible and new iterations require substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ray Bradbury Award definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ray Bradbury Award for Outstanding Dramatic Presentation: Dramatic works of any length such as motion pictures, television, Internet, radio, audio, and stage productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance/dramatic works across media may be placed in this category; serial episodes or whole arcs can be nominated as discrete works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comics category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Comics: A science fiction or fantasy story of any length told using sequential art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade collections and web/digital comics with a complete story arc can be considered eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry category definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry: A science fiction or fantasy poem of any length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-poem sequences may be nominated in part or whole; individual parts and whole are treated as discrete eligible works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic geographic/language eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All works first published in English, in the United States, during the calendar year, in the genres of science fiction, fantasy, or a related fiction genre are eligible for the Nebula Awards® in their respective categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the default eligibility window (calendar year) and language/location requirement for works to be eligible for that Nebula year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet/electronic publication treated as US publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Works first published in English on the Internet or in electronic form widely available to US readers during the calendar year shall be treated as though published in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that online/electronic availability to US readers counts as US publication for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word counts for translated works
rubrics_metrics.description: Word counts for translated works shall be based on the English word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translated works become eligible upon first publication in the English language in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of audiobooks/podcasts and similar works
rubrics_metrics.description: Works such as audiobooks, podcasts, and similar type works shall be placed in an existing category as deemed appropriate by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner, based on their word or page count and other qualities as determined by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner discretion governs which text category such media fit into; performance podcasts may be placed in Bradbury category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of performance works
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance works such as dramatic podcasts may, in the judgment of the Commissioner, be placed in the Bradbury category rather than text categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner determines category placement for works where format/performance suggests Bradbury is more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication availability rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All works that are published and available to the public in a calendar year will be taken as eligible for that calendar year for purposes of the Nebula awards, regardless of the issue date on the cover or other label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to public availability during the calendar year, not cover/label issue dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible: not yet released / limited access
rubrics_metrics.description: Works not yet released to the general public, including but not limited to: review copies for a forthcoming work, works published in a password protected or limited distribution workshop, or games published as early-access, shall not be eligible for nomination or the final ballot until the work is actually released and available to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early or limited distribution does not confer eligibility until general public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership not required for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are eligible whether or not their authors are members of SFWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFWA membership is not a prerequisite for a work to be nominated or win.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior non-U.S. publication allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are eligible whether or not they have been previously published outside of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous foreign publication does not disqualify a work from Nebula eligibility provided it meets publication-in-English-in-US rules for the relevant year (see translations clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credited writer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be eligible for any award, the work must include at least one (1) credited writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credited writer must be associated with the work to receive eligibility; this ties eligibility to credited authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-generated content prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that are written, either wholly or partially, by generative large language model (LLM) tools are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute ineligibility for works written wholly or in part by generative LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM usage disclosure and disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that used LLMs at any point during the writing process must disclose this upon acceptance of the nomination, and those works will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If LLM usage is discovered at acceptance-of-nomination stage, disclosure is required but the work will be disqualified — disclosure does not preserve eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works by awards administrators ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Works published by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner, assistants to the Nebula Awards® Commissioner or by any SFWA staff, contractors, or volunteers who possess administrative access to the Nebula Awards® nomination ballot or final ballot during the awards year shall not be eligible for nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative access to nomination/final ballots renders works ineligible to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/editor/publisher/agent may not nominate their own works
rubrics_metrics.description: Works may not be nominated by their authors, editors, publishers, or agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those with a direct professional interest in a work are disallowed from submitting nominations for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested reading database and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A secure, web-based form will be provided for all classes of members to offer 'suggested reading' throughout the year. ANY class of member will be eligible to add entries to this database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reading is a courtesy to share works of interest; entries are checked monthly for duplicates/errors by the Commissioner; works on the list are not the only eligible works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on slating and reciprocal voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deliberate strategic coordination of nominations by sub-groups of voters for the purpose of placing one or more specific works on the final ballot (also known as slating) is prohibited. Reciprocal voting or vote-trading among individual voters (also known as logrolling) is also prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballot manipulation undermines the awards; violations may result in votes being removed, works being removed from eligibility, and future eligibility impacts; appeals available to SARC and Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and appeals for voting/rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Votes shown to have been influenced by a violation of these rules may be removed at the Nebula Awards® Commissioner’s discretion. In extreme cases the Nebula Awards® Commissioner may remove a work from eligibility, and subsequent violations may impact eligibility for the Nebula Awards in future years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner will attempt to notify affected creators and appeals may be made to SARC and then to the Board; Board decisions are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination period timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The official NOMINATION PERIOD will remain open for at least six weeks and should begin no later than December 15th and extend through at least January 31st of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the minimum length and suggested start/end dates for the nomination window for the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: How nominations are submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations will be accepted via a secure online form. Voting eligible members may request a paper ballot from the Nebula Awards® Commissioner up to two weeks prior to the close of the ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper ballots must be received by the Commissioner no later than the closing date; nominations made by paper ballot will override any online submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may nominate during nomination period
rubrics_metrics.description: All Full, Associate, and Senior members (including lifetime and family members) of SFWA in good standing are eligible to make nominations during the NOMINATION PERIOD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership classes eligible to nominate are explicitly limited to these classes in good standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-member nomination limits and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each eligible member may nominate no more than five different works per category and may not nominate any work more than once. Nominations shall be treated as confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps per member per category and confidentiality protect the integrity of the nomination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting nominations and composing final ballot
rubrics_metrics.description: The nominations will be counted by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner, who shall compose the FINAL BALLOT. The FINAL BALLOT shall comprise the top six works in each category that receive the most nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner responsibility includes tallying nominations and producing the top-six final ballot per category (subject to tie rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final ballot size adjustments (zero or fewer than six nominations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that zero (0) works are nominated in a given category, then no award shall be given in that category. In the event that fewer than six (6) works are nominated in a given category, then all works will be listed on the FINAL BALLOT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no nominations are received, no award; if fewer than six, every nominated work appears on final ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie handling for final ballot additions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a tie for the final place in a category, all tied works will be added to the FINAL BALLOT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties at the cutoff expand the final ballot rather than using tie-breakers at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final ballot availability timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The FINAL BALLOT shall be made available for viewing within no more than fourteen (14) days following the close of nominations. The FINAL BALLOT shall be made available for voting within no more than one month following the close of nominations via a secure online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets explicit timelines for publishing the final ballot and opening voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may vote on final ballot
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Full, Associate, and Senior members (including lifetime and family members) in good standing shall be eligible to vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility to vote mirrors eligibility to nominate; voting rights are limited to these membership classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting process, paper ballots, and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting will be open for a minimum of one month. Voting eligible members may request a paper ballot from the Nebula Awards® Commissioner up to two weeks prior to the close of the ballot. Paper ballots must be received by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner no later than the closing date of the ballot. Votes shall be treated as confidential information. No more than one vote may be cast per category, per member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper ballots override online submissions; confidentiality and one-vote-per-member-per-category are enforced; minimum voting window is one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote tally timing and winner determination
rubrics_metrics.description: All votes will be tallied within 48 hours following the close of the FINAL BALLOT. The work in each category that receives the most votes will be declared the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick tally requirement (within 48 hours) and plurality wins (most votes) determine winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie resolution after voting
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a tie after voting on the FINAL BALLOT, the total number of nominations received for each work will determine the winner. If the number of nominations is also tied, then the tie shall stand, and all such tied works shall receive the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie-breaker sequence: (1) compare total nominations received; (2) if still tied, award is shared and tie stands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award presentation and multi-author trophy/certificate rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The winners of the Nebula Awards® shall be announced at an annual Nebula Awards® ceremony. In the event that a multi-author work wins any of these awards, a single trophy shall be awarded and individual co-authors will each receive a certificate. Should writers of the winning multi-author work wish to order additional trophies at their own expense, arrangements may be made with SFWA staff. Translators will be treated as co-authors in this situation, also receiving a separate certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical trophy policy and provision of certificates to all credited contributors, including translators on multi-author wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel eligibility relative to previously published shorter versions
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel-length version of a previously published short story, novelette, or novella shall be eligible upon the novel’s first English-language publication in the United States. A short story, novelette, or novella based on a previously-published version of the work shall not be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands eligibility to a novelized version upon first US English novel publication, but bars reusing previously short-form work as eligible in shorter forms if based on prior published material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issued novels and expanded/modified editions
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel re-issued in expanded or modified form shall not be eligible unless previously withdrawn in accordance with the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issues don't regain eligibility unless the prior edition was properly withdrawn under withdrawal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial works nomination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Serialized novels may be nominated in part or in whole. An individually published part (chapter, section, episode, etc…) of a serialized novel or a complete serialized novel in whole will be treated as discrete works, separately eligible, and nominations will be tallied for each separately. Nothing shall preclude one part of a series and the entirety of the serialized novel as a whole from appearing together on the final ballot. Serialized novels may include multi-author compilations consisting of separately published parts written by different authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serialized publications create discrete eligible units; both parts and whole can appear simultaneously; multi-author serialized compilations are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game writing new iteration eligibility and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A new iteration of a game (often, but not always referred to as 'version' or 'edition') shall be eligible provided substantive changes have been made to content, gameplay, or story. Decisions regarding the eligibility of new iterations of a game will be made by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner with support from the Game Writing Committee. Decisions may be appealed to the Board. Board decisions will be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive content/gameplay/story changes are required for eligibility of new game iterations; Commissioner + Game Writing Committee decide, with Board appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic presentation episode/arc rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Serial works may be nominated by individual episode or in whole. An individual episode of a dramatic series or a complete story arc of multiple episodes will be treated as discrete works, separately eligible, and nominations will be tallied for each separately. Nothing shall preclude an individual episode of a series and the entirety of a story arc from appearing together on the final ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes and arcs are discrete eligible works and can both appear on ballots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comics trade and webcomic eligibility specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible works for this award shall be any science fiction or fantasy story-driven narrative told using sequential art of any length. A Trade (collection of serialized single issue comics) can be considered in this category. A web or digital comic can be considered in this category if it contains a complete story arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both collected trades and complete web/digital arcs can be eligible as comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry multi-part and multi-author rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-poem sequences may be nominated in part or in whole. An individually published part of a multi-part poem or a complete multi-part poem in whole will be treated as discrete works, separately eligible, and nominations will be tallied for each separately. Nothing shall preclude one part of a multi-part poem and the entirety of the multi-part poem as a whole from appearing together on the final ballot. Multi-part poems may include multi-author compilations consisting of separately published parts written by different authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-part poems and multi-author poem compilations are treated analogously to serialized/series rules: parts and whole can both be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal grounds and process (temporary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of any eligible work may withdraw it from consideration in a given year and request that a later edition be considered for the Nebula Awards®, but only in two specific cases: If the work appeared as a limited edition publication, or; If the author finds the published version unacceptable as the result of editorial changes or production errors. An author must present a written request for withdrawal to the Nebula Awards® Commissioner by November 1 or within thirty (30) days after the publication, production, or broadcast of the work, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal requests for later consideration are narrowly permitted and must be timely and written. Nominations already on file will not be carried over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement, permanent withdrawal, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: For a later edition of a withdrawn work to be eligible, the author must present a written request for reinstatement to the Nebula Awards® Commissioner. Nominations shall not be accepted for a work withdrawn from eligibility. Nominations on file for any such work will not be carried over to the future. An author may permanently withdraw a work from eligibility by delivering a written request to the Nebula Awards® Commissioner. No work so withdrawn shall ever again be eligible for the Nebula Awards®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes temporary withdrawal+reinstatement from permanent withdrawal which permanently eliminates eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-year withdrawal effect on existing nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a work published late in the year is withdrawn after November 1st and has received nominations, those nominations will be null and void. An attempt will be made to notify member(s) who nominated the work so that they may submit replacement nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawals after Nov 1 nullify nominations and nominators should be notified to submit replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner and SARC appointments and recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The SFWA President shall ... appoint a Nebula Awards® Commissioner ... and a three (3) person SFWA Awards Rules Committee (SARC). Members of the SFWA Awards Rules Committee (SARC) who appear on the FINAL BALLOT must recuse themselves from any subsequent vote that concerns eligibility or interpretation of rules in the category in which they appear for that year’s Nebula awards. The Nebula Awards® Commissioner will serve as a secretary to the SFWA Awards Rules Committee (SARC), but shall not be a voting member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments are presidential; SARC members on final ballot must recuse from related rule/eligibility votes to prevent conflicts; Commissioner is non-voting SARC secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board recusal and appeal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members who appear on the FINAL BALLOT must recuse themselves from any subsequent Board vote that concerns eligibility or interpretation of rules for that year’s Nebula, Bradbury, or Norton Awards. If an author, a director, or writer of a dramatic production, or the responsible party for a playable or interactive work disagrees with a decision made by the SARC, he or she may apply to the Board of Directors for a further appeal by presenting to them a brief summary of the reasons for the appeal. At this time, the SARC shall provide a summary of their decision to the Board. If two members of the Board then believe that an appeal is justified, the decision shall be voted on by the Board, which may overrule the SARC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a multi-step appeal path (Commissioner -> SARC -> Board) and recusal rules for Board members who appear on the final ballot; Board may overrule SARC with vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule interpretation authority and notification effort
rubrics_metrics.description: The interpretation of these rules, and all questions regarding eligibility, withdrawals, nominations, ballots, etc. shall be decided by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner, subject to appeal to the SARC. In the event of an appeal, an effort will be made to contact the creator or creators of the work in question and inform them of any decisions regarding eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has primary interpretive authority with formal appeal channels and a duty to attempt notification of creators affected by decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to create additional categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The SFWA Board of Directors, with a two thirds supermajority vote, may create additional categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board has the formal power to expand award categories by supermajority vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper ballot precedence over online submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper ballots must be received by the Nebula Awards® Commissioner no later than the closing date of the ballot. Nominations made by paper ballot will override any online submissions. Votes made by paper ballot will override any online submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper submissions take precedence over online ones for both nominations and final voting; provides a mechanism for accommodating members without online access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency timing constraint for rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall make every attempt to avoid changing the rules during the active period of nomination or voting to increase clarity, but acknowledges that on occasion it may be unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board should avoid mid-cycle rule changes; if changes are necessary they may happen but should be minimal and avoided where possible.
